WHAT WE'RE BUILDING NEXT

The Performance Institute.

A first-of-its-kind partnership between Axis Bank and GoSports Foundation, building India's premier hub for sports science, athlete testing, and applied research — housed at the Centre for Sports Excellence, Bengaluru.

Partner on this initiative
₹40 CrProposed outlay, FY 26–27 to FY 29–30
800+Target athletes

BengaluruAt the Centre for Sports Excellence
Purpose

The backbone institution for Indian sport

Elite sporting success is not a solitary pursuit. Systems of winning bridge the thin margins of victory through science, strategy, and support — for the individual athlete and the national team alike.

The Performance Institute aims to become the internationally-renowned backbone institution that leads and measures the performance of India's sports ecosystem: enhancing talent identification, safeguarding athlete well-being, driving inclusive participation, and strengthening domestic coaching and sports science capacity.

[ Render needed: Performance Institute laboratory building, CSE Bengaluru ]
The model

Three integrated pillars

01

People

Build India's coaching, sports science, and governance pipeline — training programmes, fellowships, mentorship, and professional development pathways for practitioners across federations, academies, and high-performance environments.

02

Analytics

Establish India's premier athlete testing, assessment, and strategy facility — performance testing, biomechanics, recovery monitoring, injury-risk assessment, and data-driven performance planning.

03

Research

Create a national repository of indigenous data sets, sports science research, and innovation — generating India-specific evidence rather than relying on foreign benchmarks.

Why this, why now

Three gaps in India's sporting landscape

A shortage of India-specific data sets and research infrastructure limits sports science adoption, leaving coaches dependent on foreign benchmarks. There have been only 16 India-specific studies covering 887 athletes over 20 years, and 58% of athletes report under-use of sports science support — adoption is weakest outside elite training environments.

Athlete support systems remain thin compared to global standards. Globally, elite athletes have 8–12 specialists supporting them; India averages roughly 1 support staff per Olympic athlete, with many coaches playing multiple roles. In daily training settings, support is often 1 expert per 4–5 athletes at National Camps and above.

Indian junior athletes show high promise, but early specialisation locks them into one sport before true aptitude is understood. Just 3–4% transition from junior to senior athletics (vs. 20–30% globally); multi-sport participation has fallen to 1.6 sports/year (down from 2.2); and 1 in 5 athletes trains in a primary sport 9–12 months a year.

Coach-to-athlete ratio

1:114 in India vs. an ideal global standard of 1:10. At Paris 2024, 25 of 68 coaches (37%) were foreign — reflecting a domestic capacity gap.

Sanctioned vs. employed coaches

The Sports Authority of India employs just 860 of 1,524 sanctioned coaching positions — a 43% vacancy rate.

India's 1.4 billion population fuels immense sporting passion, yet only 10% have played a sport, and Sport & Physical Activity contributes just 0.1% of GDP and 0.5% of jobs today. By 2047, that could grow to 2% of GDP and 4% of jobs.

Policy alignment

Built for where national policy is heading

National Sports Policy 2025

Khelo Bharat Niti — excellence on the global stage, sport for economic & social development, and integration with education (NEP 2020).

Khelo India Mission 2026

Integrated talent development pathways, systematic coach & support staff development, and sports science & technology integration.

Union Budget 2026

Enhanced investment in sports science infrastructure, professionalisation of the sports workforce, and incentives for sports manufacturing.

Roadmap

From current state to 2030 outcomes

People

Expert onboarding → periodic certification batches → national & global accreditation.

By 2030: 300 certified coaches & experts, industry-ready talent for government and private sector roles.

Analytics

Establish testing facility → pilot athlete testing for talent ID → scale to enhance on-field performance.

By 2030: 1,000 athletes tested with Fit-to-Sport profiling, 200 elite athletes tested, reduced burnout and injury risk.

Research

Define priority research areas → build institute partnerships → structured data capture.

By 2030: Athlete Management System developed, publications in international sports science journals.

The facility

Centre for Sports Excellence (CSE)

A 16-acre, fully integrated high-performance sports hub in Bengaluru, offering world-class training and competition infrastructure across numerous sports. An MoU between GoSports Foundation and CSE is already in place for the proposed facility — a building currently used as a Sports Museum, showcasing memorabilia from Indian athletes.

Vivek Kumar

Founder & Director, CSE. A three-time Karnataka State Badminton champion and co-founder of the Prakash Padukone Badminton Academy.

Ved Kumar

Managing Director, CSE. Brings global sport management experience, shaping CSE into a world-class private sports ecosystem.

Governance

How it's structured

An Advisory Board provides strategic guidance and sectoral expertise; the Director leads execution, oversees functional heads, and drives cross-team accountability.

Advisory Board

Axis Bank representative · GoSports Foundation representative · CSE representative · Independent representative

Institute Director

Leads execution across three functional heads: Head of People, Head of Analytics, and Head of Research.

Sustainability

From founding partner to self-sustaining institution

Project Cycle 1 (Years 1–4, FY 2026–30) is primarily funded by Axis Bank as Founding Partner, ensuring clear governance, operational stability, and strong brand association while the institute develops capability to onboard new partners. The aim is for AGTPI to become self-sustaining by the completion of Project Cycle 2 (Years 5–8, 2030–2034).

Why GoSports leads this

Built on 18 years in the field

GoSports Foundation, established as a Trust in 2008, is a professionally managed, national award-winning, independent non-profit — an acknowledged leader in designing and implementing multi-year sports excellence and development programmes.

John Gloster

Director of Sports Science

Australian physiotherapist with decades of elite cricket experience since the late 1990s; former Head Physio of the Indian national cricket team (2005–2008), working with captains Ganguly, Dravid, Kumble, and Dhoni. Part of GoSports since 2014, he built the Sports Science vertical and established its protocols.
